applicability.defect: triangle or ngon appearing at a beveled corner

preconditions: bevel_selection (typed op) or a Bevel modifier/edit-mode operator is applied to edges that meet at one vertex where 3 or more edges converge
the resulting corner cap topology matters (feeds Subdivision Surface, or must stay all-quad for a production asset)
required_observations: per-face vertex count on the evaluated/base mesh at the corner in question -- NOT this project's own mesh_health.ngons field, which was found live to count only faces with 5+ vertices and silently excludes triangles (confirmed: an 8-triangle all-edges-beveled cube reported ngons: 0)
whether ALL edges meeting at the corner are included in the same bevel selection, or only some of them
action_policy: The source claim (McGlasham SubD series, video BmxF8gBSKmQ, CAPTURED transcript-only) was: odd Bevel segment count always creates a triangle at a corner, even count 'keeps the corner all-quad'. Live-reproduced in this project's own typed pipeline (bevel_selection): the triangle-vs-no-triangle half of the claim is CONFIRMED exactly -- segments=1 on a 3-edge cube corner produced exactly one triangle (face_vertex_counts: {3:1, 4:6, 5:3}); segments=2 on the same corner produced zero triangles ({4:12, 6:3}).

The 'all-quad' half of the claim is FALSE as literally stated and was corrected by transfer testing on different geometry. A single isolated 3-edge corner beveled with segments=2 (only those 3 edges selected, the other 9 cube edges untouched) still left 3 hexagonal (6-vertex) faces at that corner -- not all-quad. Only when ALL 12 edges of the cube were beveled together (segments=2) did the result become genuinely all-quad (54 quads, 0 triangles, 0 ngons of any size).

Correct, tested rule: even segment count reliably eliminates the TRIANGLE at a multi-edge corner regardless of selection scope. Whether the corner is ALSO fully quad (vs. leaving a small ngon) additionally depends on whether every edge meeting at that vertex is included in the same bevel pass -- partial-selection corners are more likely to leave a residual ngon even with even segments.

Practical guidance for this project's typed surface: when calling bevel_selection near a corner, prefer selecting all edges converging on that vertex in one call rather than beveling edges individually or in partial groups, and always pass an even segments value (2 is enough for the triangle-elimination effect; higher values add roundness, not correctness).
expected_effects: Odd segments (1, 3, 5, ...) on edges meeting at an N-valence corner (N>=3): exactly one triangle face at that corner, confirmed at N=3.
Even segments (2, 4, ...) on the SAME edges: zero triangles at that corner, but the cap face may still be an ngon (N-1 or fewer vertices) if not all edges at the vertex were included in the bevel.
Even segments AND all edges at the vertex included in one bevel pass: genuinely all-quad result at that corner.
success_predicates: face_vertex_counts (per-face len(verts) on the actual bmesh, not the aggregate ngons field) contains no 3-vertex faces at the target corner after an even-segment bevel
for a fully all-quad requirement: face_vertex_counts at the corner contains only 4-vertex faces, achieved by beveling every edge meeting at that vertex together with an even segment count
failure_predicates: any 3-vertex face present at a beveled corner after checking real per-face vertex counts (this project's mesh_health.ngons alone will not catch this -- confirmed live, it does not count triangles)
assuming even segments alone guarantees an all-quad corner without checking whether all edges at that vertex were included in the same bevel selection
recovery: re-run bevel_selection with an even segments value (2 is sufficient to remove the triangle)
if a residual ngon remains at the corner after an even-segment bevel, re-select and bevel ALL edges meeting at that vertex together in one call, rather than the partial set originally selected

experiments.description: Two fresh cubes (BevelTestOdd, BevelTestEven). On each, the 3 edges meeting at one corner (agent_ids 14,15,17) were selected and bevel_selection(offset=0.3, segments=1) vs segments=2 applied. Per-face vertex counts queried directly via bmesh: segments=1 -> {3:1, 4:6, 5:3} (one triangle); segments=2 -> {4:12, 6:3} (zero triangles, but three hexagonal ngons remain since only 3 of the corner's edges were beveled, not all of them). Wireframe isometric render (wireframe_odd_vs_even.png) visually confirms a single sharp facet on the odd case and a more filled, rounder corner on the even case.
experiments.limitation: Single 3-valence corner only; offset=0.3 on a size-2 cube.

experiments.description: Two more fresh cubes (BevelTestFullOdd, BevelTestFullEven), this time beveling ALL 12 edges (every corner, all edges per corner) at once: segments=1 -> {3:8, 4:18} (exactly one triangle per corner, 8 total, matching the 8 corners); segments=2 -> {4:54} (zero triangles, zero ngons of any size -- genuinely all-quad). This is the transfer that corrected the source's 'all-quad' claim: it only holds when every edge at a vertex is beveled together, which full-object bevel does automatically but a partial/single-corner selection does not. Wireframe isometric render (wireframe_full_odd_vs_even.png) confirms visually.
experiments.limitation: Still primitive cube geometry (90-degree corners only); not yet tested on a non-orthogonal multi-edge corner (e.g. a hexagonal prism apex) or via the Bevel modifier (object-level) as opposed to bevel_selection (edit-mode/typed op).

planner_hint.expected_effect: Zero triangle faces at the target corner; all-quad result if the ticket's edge selection already covers every edge meeting at that vertex.
verification: query real per-face vertex counts at the target corner (not mesh_health.ngons, which does not count triangles)
confirm 0 faces with exactly 3 vertices at the corner
if any face there has 5+ vertices, confirm every edge meeting at that vertex was included in operation_params' edge selection
